commit.message:
ci: run the live suites in parallel, each run in its own namespace, with no lock (#3841)

## What

Removes the `linear-live-documents` concurrency group from `ci.yml`
(`check`, `test-linux`) and `linear-documents.yml`, and makes every live
session independent of every other run:

- **GitHub:** each session copies the nominated board #1 with
`copyProjectV2` (fields, `Status` options, draft items), runs its whole
journey on the copy, and deletes it however it ends. Board #1 becomes a
template no session writes to; `just github-live-template dry-run|fill`
fills its drafts (done: 60).
- **Linear:** the team keeps a pool of 16 standing slot sets per lane,
and each run leases one. A lease is an issue created under an id derived
from the member and its generation. Linear refuses a second create under
an existing id, and every claim re-sends that create and requires
Linear's recorded refusal (`INPUT_ERROR`, "conflict on insert of Issue",
"Entity Issue with id … already exists."). Any other answer fails
closed. Leases are released on every way out. `just linear-document-pool
dry-run|initialize` fills the pool (done in TES2: 80 slots present).
- **Namespace guards:** each lane refuses, before sending, a request
naming another run's board or record. This covers the lane's own
requests, the Linear plugin source and the Linear asset binary (through
the relays they are pointed at). The GitHub pair's double fails on any
request naming the template after the copy, the plugin source's
included.
- **Cancellation:** `test-linux` now runs the cancellation cleanup
`check` had. Both credentialed jobs also release the Linear leases they
recorded (`janitor --linear --release-leases`), each only while it still
reads back as recorded.
- **Janitor:** removes CI-stamped board copies once their run reads
completed, never board #1 or an unstamped board.
- **Guard test:** `policy.test.mjs` fails if a concurrency group returns
on a job or workflow that runs a live suite.

## Limits and how each is kept

| Limit | How |
|---|---|
| GitHub fields per board (50), item counts, origin field | Per run: its
own board |
| GitHub GraphQL, 5,000 points/hour | Each run's design allocation is
343 + 112 points; eight runs fit the 80% the retained buffer leaves |
| GitHub content creations, 500/hour | About 30 per run |
| GitHub per-minute secondary limits (80 creations, 2,000 points) | Four
runs' 18-creation setup bursts fit one minute and a fifth is refused.
Beyond four, overlapping runs rely on writes spread across a session and
on the plugin's backoff; no more headroom is claimed |
| Linear documents, 1,000 per team including trash | The pool bounds
them at 64, each created once |
| Linear requests (2,500/hour) and complexity (3,000,000/hour) per key |
Thirty-two runs' lease and document traffic was never refused |
| Lease pool | 16 per lane |

Every limit above is enforced in the loopback doubles as the service
enforces it.

## Not in this change

Two complete journeys of each lane run concurrently against shared
doubles: drafted as a follow-up by the manager's ruling. The
lifecycle-level concurrency tests here, plus the hosted overlapping-run
proof, stand in for it.

## Notes

- Builds on #3811 and #3821's standing slots.
- `scripts/check-live-janitor.sh`, `check-live-lane.sh` and
`check-live-lane-selection.sh` now hold four cancellation steps, two
commands, rather than one.
- Session-cost golden: 240 requests on top of main's 233. Design
allocations: setup 14→22, schema 10→12, assets 85→91. Janitor request
budget 20→21. `github-live-session-points` stays at 299.
- An earlier push of this branch was a raw `git push`; it is republished
here through `onevcs publish`.

commit.message:
fix(ci): adopt the budget figures script that spends no read on a skipped run (#3845)

## What

Skip jobs reads for workflow runs concluded skipped, bringing v0.13.0’s
release read count from 7 to 6 without changing any budget thresholds.
The figures script is byte-identical to [dero-skills’ landing commit
d12c819](https://github.com/nickderobertis/dero-skills/commit/d12c819d6a160d7fe2756d8333b8a735195e5989).

Add recorded-release regression coverage for delivery-run selection and
preserve the PR job contract: lint, Linux and Windows always run; macOS
skips only same-repository `release-plz-*` PRs.

## Why

CI and CD budgets must reflect actual work. A release that published
every artifact should not read red because its measurement fetched jobs
for a workflow that ran nothing.

## Additional info

The v0.13.0 fixture counts release-plz and Release, excludes the cache
warmer from every CD figure, and makes no jobs request for the skipped
Visual docs run. Its release-tail commands report all seven figures
within their unchanged thresholds:

| Budget | Fixture figure | Threshold |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| onetaskgraph-ci-check-time | 1,636 s | 1,800 s |
| onetaskgraph-cd-job-time | 954 s | 1,800 s |
| onetaskgraph-release-cycle-time | 5,323 s | 5,400 s |
| onetaskgraph-ci-job-count | 4 | 4 |
| onetaskgraph-cd-job-count | 6 | 6 |
| onetaskgraph-release-read-requests | 6 | 6 |
| onetaskgraph-pr-read-requests | 2 | 2 |

The fixture fixes the clock at the tail step’s start. The original
[v0.13.0 Release
run](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph/actions/runs/41252264998)
measured release-cycle time later in that step at 5,329 s, within 5,400
s with 71 s headroom. No release-cycle change is included.

---------

Co-authored-by: Nick DeRobertis <19440155+nickderobertis@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
fix(ci): run the npm publish check from a copy, not the checkout (#3846)

## What

Completes
[#3841](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph/pull/3841), which
isolated the live lanes and removed the `linear-live-documents` lock.
The npm-publish check now uses a scratch copy, protecting the checkout’s
TypeScript build output from concurrent checks, with a regression guard
enforcing that protection. Also corrects Nx tag-pattern handling in the
workflow placement guard and documents the live template board’s
required contents.

## Why

Pull-request Linux jobs must finish within 30 minutes without waiting
behind other runs’ live tests. The shared lock previously added
6,577–9,114 seconds of queueing. With isolation already on main, this
completes the work by fixing a checkout race exposed by parallel checks
and preserving the faster existing phase layout.

## Additional info

**Checkout protection.** The npm-publish check previously created a
stand-in `sdks/typescript/dist` and removed it on exit, potentially
deleting a real build produced concurrently by
`github-workflows:cd-journeys`. The resulting `ENOENT` occurred in
[41266553208](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph/actions/runs/41266553208)
and in
[41245850140](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph/actions/runs/41245850140),
an unrelated branch running main’s code; main was exposed too. The new
guard runs the check in a clone without `dist` and refuses changes to
the SDK directory. Against the old script it fails on the directory’s
changed mtime. It adds about 17 seconds to `scripts:test`.

The placement guard now handles trailing `*` in tags and `!tag:`
reinclusion, including main’s `tag:test-in-coverage:*` exclusion.

**Final-head timing.** All required jobs (`lint`, `test-linux`,
`test-macos`, `test-windows`) passed in both overlapping executions. The
trees at `f36d4ff1` and final head `01fa542f` are identical; the latter
is an empty commit.

| Phase |
[41271824631](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph/actions/runs/41271824631)
|
[41271834160](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph/actions/runs/41271834160)
| [Main-code baseline
41207786578](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph/actions/runs/41207786578)
|
|---|---|---|---|
| test-linux total | 15m57 | 17m28 | 23.7 min |
| Main test | 11m10 | 11m54 | 22m07 |
| Coverage | 13m40 | 15m30 | 17m01 |
| Distribution test | 14m56 | 16m25 | 15m16 |
| Distribution check | 3m48 | 4m54 | — |

Most of the difference is affected selection, not a speed improvement:
the final diff selects `scripts`, `workspace` and
`github-workflow-policy`, with no crate test, live lane or
`github-workflows:cd-journeys` selected. No test was removed, skipped or
moved, no timeout was raised, and the registered
`onetaskgraph-ci-check-time` budget remains 1,800 seconds.

**Why the phase split was dropped.** Separate live-lane phases increased
CPU contention on the four-core runner. These are the measured Nx phase
durations; test-linux’s final phases and parallelism are unchanged from
main.

| Run | Layout | test-linux | Main test | Coverage | Distribution test |
GitHub lane | Linear lane |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|
[41258284271](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph/actions/runs/41258284271)
(#3841) | Main’s | Pass 25m23 | 24m12 | 20m12 | 17m38 | Inside main |
15m03 |
|
[41266553208](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph/actions/runs/41266553208)
| Split, coverage ×4 | Fail 29m38: ENOENT | 27m06 | 27m57 | 26m15 | Pass
25m17 | Pass 22m01 |
|
[41266524030](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph/actions/runs/41266524030)
| Split, coverage ×4 | Cancelled 30m41 | Unfinished | Unfinished |
Unfinished | Phase unfinished; live journey passed | Asset journey
cancelled at cap |
|
[41269339059](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph/actions/runs/41269339059)
| Split, main ×2 | Cancelled at cap | 29m38 | 27m43 | 23m41 | Pass 25m26
| Pass 19m58 |
|
[41269330442](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph/actions/runs/41269330442)
| Split, main ×2 | Cancelled at cap | Unfinished | Unfinished | 28m38 |
Pass 28m11 | Pass 22m03 |

Reducing the main phase’s slots produced a 29-minute serial chain
through policy tests, rust-cache-action, release-tail, janitor, scripts
and workspace tests. Restoring main’s layout removed that added
contention. The ENOENT failure is addressed here; the other incomplete
jobs hit the unchanged timeout under the discarded layout, while the
cited main-layout baseline passed.

**Hosted isolation evidence.** The four split-layout executions above
overlapped in pairs started 27 and 7 seconds apart. GitHub’s live
journey and copied-board preflight passed in all four. Linear passed in
41266553208, 41269330442 and 41269339059; 41266524030 was cancelled
during its asset journey, and cancellation released its pool lease. None
encountered a lease, board or limit refusal. Copied-board setup took
44.7–51.3 seconds and 48–53 requests; GitHub’s live journey took 832–864
seconds. These executions supply the live overlap proof; the final-head
pair supplies the timing proof.

**Template and limits.** Template board #1 was verified with 60 drafts
among 63 items, within the documented 51–90 draft requirement. Only
drafts reach a copied board, and preflight counts that copy. Each
session uses `copyProjectV2`, writes only to its own copy and deletes it
on exit. The janitor targets run boards and exact CI-stamped artifacts
belonging to completed runs, never template drafts. Runs cannot drain
the template; the earlier drain was manual.

#3841 contains the resource isolation and registered limit workload.
Linear reuses a 16-member document pool because its document limit
includes trash; leases prevent concurrent ownership and are released on
success, failure and cancellation. Scheduled Linear cleanup retains only
`LINEAR_API_KEY` and `LINEAR_WRITE_TEAM`, recovering abandoned stamped
documents by age; the lane reclaims pool leases under its completed-run
rule.

GitHub’s secondary ceiling is 80 content creations per minute. One
session’s measured setup creates 18 objects—nine issues and nine board
items—so four overlapping setup bursts fit (72), while five do not (90).
No headroom beyond four is claimed. Existing limit backoff remains, with
no fixed pacing; temporary-conflict responses also use that backoff,
covered against the doubles.

**Follow-ups:** a multi-board GitHub double, a full Linear capability
double, and two concurrent complete journeys of each lane against shared
doubles. Existing concurrency coverage proves ownership and cleanup at
the shared-resource level.

No headroom beyond four is claimed. Existing limit backoff remains, with
no fixed pacing; temporary-conflict responses also use that backoff,
covered against the doubles.

double, and two concurrent complete journeys of each lane against shared
doubles. Existing concurrency coverage proves ownership and cleanup at

commit.message:
fix(linear): retire standing live-test identities no current lane owns (#3848)

## What

Fix Linear live-lane discovery refusing stray retained identities with
`unknown standing ownership; discovery required before initialization`:
unparsed document titles and project names are now ignored. The
scheduled janitor also retires the nominated team’s superseded pre-pool
CI documents and parent project once each has been untouched for more
than 24 hours.

## Why

Several managers share the same Linear test workspace. Leftover standing
objects from one manager blocked another’s live tests and required
manual API deletion. Discovery and cleanup now handle that residue
without disturbing another run’s standing identities.

## Additional info

The janitor deletes superseded documents before their parent and keeps
the parent while any such document remains. Current pool slots, lease
issues, local standing sets, other teams’ sets, and unparsed
retained/lease titles remain protected. Unparsed identities are ignored,
not retired; AGENTS.md records these boundaries.

Replay regressions cover the reproduced discovery failure, concurrent
plugin sessions, the real asset journey, preservation of other runs’
identities, and janitor retirement followed by an empty second pass.

commit.message:
fix: set up GitHub project fields with the inputs GitHub accepts (#3842)

## What

Fix GitHub Projects field setup so missing Status options and Priority
can be configured without changing existing items’ status or priority.
Both GitHub test doubles now validate requests and variables against
GitHub’s complete published schema, including regressions for the
invalid 0.12.13 request and malformed or adversarial documents.

Raise the three pull-request test jobs’ execution limits from 30 to 40
minutes, preserving other job limits. Repair distribution fixture
handling, the Linear budget journal’s producer dependency, and
timing-sensitive test assertions.

## Why

Open action items across manager sessions need to reach the user’s
human-task boards. GitHub rejected an unsupported `projectId` in the
Status update, blocking setup before Priority could be created. The
previous test double accepted that invalid request and let the defect
ship. Passing CI runs also approached the old execution limit, causing
ordinary timing variance to cancel checks.

## Additional info

Validation uses vendored, pinned graphql-js under Bun; apollo-compiler
would require dependency-policy exceptions for duplicate transitive
dependencies. The complete schema’s published source, retrieval date,
Last-Modified value and digest are recorded beside it. One schema-level
deprecation rule violated by GitHub’s published file is tolerated;
request validation remains enabled in full. Regressions cover duplicate,
unknown and missing input fields, fragment cycles, selection merging,
undefined variables and adversarial documents.

A shared validator server reuses schema and document validation across
test processes. Tests cover idle shutdown, replacement after a watched
file changes, and refusal of malformed command lines or
`GITHUB_SCHEMA_IDLE_MS`. Distribution fixtures include and resolve the
validator, and its generated files stay under `target/`.

The primary-reset pacing assertion now accounts for the wall-clock
seconds the command spans. The Linear pool-lease test from
[#3841](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph/pull/3841) now
rejects overlapping holds of the same member while allowing reuse after
release. Its former assertion caused the [test-windows
failure](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph/actions/runs/41293164371/job/124808443064).
A mutation treating a refused lease claim as won still fails with
“assets-0-0 and assets-0-1 held Assets member 16 at once”; all 205
unmutated Linear tests passed. No Linear production code changed, and a
follow-up asks the live-suite owners to review the assertion.

On `dd550ec1`, one same-host round of the four affected test projects
took **146.4 seconds**, with all **1,831 tests passing**. Base
`3e902a74` took **141.1, 133.3 and 134.9 seconds** over three rounds,
averaging **136.4 seconds**: **+7.3%**, below the 15% limit.

Earlier timing evidence remains historical:

- Against `3e902a74`, three rounds totaled **409.2 seconds at base →
402.2 seconds on `b2431911`** (ratio 0.983). Both trees had intermittent
failures; these totals do not establish an all-green suite or a speedup.
- Against `3e902a74`, **377.0 → 358.4 seconds** on `15766fa9`, with all
24 runs passing.
- Against `1c80fdcc`, **133.7 → 136.6 seconds** with nextest (+2.2%) and
**202.2 → 208.3 seconds** with cargo test (+3.0%), including a
successful baseline rerun after an allowance-read connection failure.

Recorded local checks on `dd550ec1` passed: `just distribution-check`,
`just distribution-test`, diff-scoped llmlint and its config validation,
clippy, and the full GitHub Projects and Linear plugin suites. Affected
formatting/lint/type checks passed on `b2431911`; after the merge,
distribution checks/tests, the uncredentialed Linear test phase and
budget, workflow guards and lint-config validation passed again. The
schema suite also passed under both runners earlier. These results do
not establish green CI; the linked Windows failure and the earlier
[test-linux
failure](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onetaskgraph/actions/runs/41285626873/job/124786214649)
predate these repairs.

Follow-ups: live setup on the two human-task boards remains in the
ai-orchestrator adoption; the reporting-only CI-time budget remains at
1800 seconds. The intermittent
`plan_copy::a_plan_copy_reads_what_the_plan_holds_whatever_the_board_has_accumulated`
failure also occurred at base
(`time-5-base-onetaskgraph-github-projects-e2e-20261101T063814Z.log`);
it passed in all six earlier comparison runs.

+## `github-schema.docs.graphql` — GitHub's complete published schema
+
+`github-schema.docs.graphql` is GitHub.com's public GraphQL schema file exactly as GitHub
+distributes it, whole and unedited: <https://docs.github.com/public/fpt/schema.docs.graphql>,
+retrieved 2026-10-31 (served `last-modified: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 10:30:11 GMT`), 1,561,946 bytes,
+SHA-256 `ee690896ae7d9126765c6a660174b40c9d1974b70db36af8559117b9c4a7b7a6`. To refresh it,
+download that URL over the file and record the new date, size and digest here.
+
+Two gates hold the copy, both in `tests/plugin.rs`. One pins it to that digest — computed by
+`validate.mjs` from the file it builds, so the check and the pin read the same bytes — so it cannot be
+edited by hand or refreshed without its provenance moving in the same change. The other
+reconciles it with every contract the credentialed lane introspects from GitHub on every run —
+each mutation's input and payload, each contract type's fields and types, each contract enum's
+members (`journey::MUTATION_CONTRACT`, `CONTRACT_TYPES`, `contract_field_types`,
+`CONTRACT_ENUMS`) — so where GitHub changes one of those contracts, either the live lane fails
+against GitHub or this reconciliation fails against the copy, and the copy is refreshed. A
+change GitHub makes elsewhere in its schema is caught only when the copy is next refreshed;
+`updateProjectV2Field`, which the field setup sends, is not among those live contracts.
+
+It is not a reduction, and that is its purpose. `schema.graphql` above is a subset written by
+the same hand as the documents it checks, and in 0.12.13 it defined `projectId` on
+`UpdateProjectV2FieldInput` — which GitHub does not — so the field setup's Status-option
+update passed both that check and the loopback board and was refused by the live API with
+`Variable $input of type UpdateProjectV2FieldInput! was provided invalid value for projectId
+(Field is not defined on UpdateProjectV2FieldInput)`. Against this file:
+
+- `tests/github_schema/mod.rs` validates a request by every rule of the GraphQL
+  specification's Validation section and coerces its variables (`CoerceVariableValues`), as
+  GitHub does before running anything, through graphql-js — the GraphQL Foundation's reference
+  implementation, run under `bun` by `tests/github_schema/validate.mjs`, since no Rust
+  validator fits this workspace's dependency policy unchanged (the module documentation says
+  which and why); `tests/schema.rs` breaks
+  each rule once and shows it refused. graphql-js 17 finds one type-system rule this file
+  breaks — an implementation field deprecated where its interface field is not, eight times
+  — which governs how a schema is written rather than what a request may ask, so that rule
+  alone is tolerated and any other schema error stops every check;
+- `tests/schema.rs` holds every document in `graphql::DOCUMENTS` to it, and the field setup's
+  requests with the variables they are sent with;
+- this crate's board (`tests/plugin.rs`) and the shared loopback board every binary journey
+  drives (`onetaskgraph-e2e-support`, which includes that module by path) refuse any request
+  it rejects, answering as GitHub does: HTTP 200, `errors`, no `data`, and changing nothing on
+  the board. The GitHub Projects e2e suite includes the module by path too, to show a
+  document the board does not answer is one GitHub runs.

+## `../github_schema/graphql-17.0.2.tgz` — graphql-js, as npm publishes it
+
+The validator's graphql-js is npm's own published tarball, committed byte for byte:
+<https://registry.npmjs.org/graphql/-/graphql-17.0.2.tgz>, retrieved 2026-10-31, 1,019,024
+bytes, integrity `sha512-FRWbddMxfkjiB7z+aQDWIR+E34xo9I8c9mtK2RPv8PmMzKRvrdsreHL/Ui/TmwHJfhHChEtsFPyMHKI+xuarQQ==`
+— the `dist.integrity` npm records for it. `validate.mjs` refuses a tarball that does not hash
+to that before unpacking anything (`tests/schema.rs` shows it refusing one byte off), then
+unpacks it once into `target/github-schema/node_modules/graphql` and imports it from there —
+under the workspace's `target` rather than beside it, so a test run changes nothing in this
+crate's directory, which a release hashes between building and publishing the crate.

+and `GRAPHQL_INTEGRITY` there to its name and `npm view graphql@<version> dist.integrity`,

+/// A malformed or adversarial request is refused, never answered by a crash or an exhausted
+/// stack: bytes that are not GraphQL, nesting far past any real document's, a fragment cycle
+/// two thousand spreads long, a wide selection, more tokens than it parses and deeply nested
+/// variables.
+#[test]
+fn a_malformed_or_adversarial_request_is_refused_rather_than_crashing() {
+    use serde_json::json;
+
+    // Each of these takes the server seconds, which would be every other test's wait too.
+    let server = github_schema::serve_privately();
+
+    let refused = |document: &str, variables: serde_json::Value| {
+        server
+            .refuse(&json!({"query": document, "variables": variables}))
+            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{} was not refused", &document[..document.len().min(80)]))
+    };
+    refused("", json!({}));
+    refused("\u{0}\u{1}garbage{{{", json!({}));
+    refused("query{viewer{login}} }}}}", json!({}));
+    let deep = |open: &str, close: &str, depth: usize| (open.repeat(depth), close.repeat(depth));
+    let (open, close) = deep("viewer{", "}", 50_000);
+    assert_eq!(
+        refused(&format!("query{{{open}login{close}}}"), json!({})),
+        json!({"errors": [{"message": "The request nests too deeply to validate."}]})
+    );
+    // A deep document that breaks no rule is validated, not refused for its depth.
+    let (open, close) = deep("ofType{", "}", 190);
+    assert_eq!(
+        server
+            .refuse(&json!({"query": format!("query{{__schema{{types{{{open}name{close}}}}}}}")})),
+        None
+    );
+    let (open, close) = deep("[", "]", 50_000);
+    assert_eq!(
+        refused(
+            &format!("query{{node(id:{open}1{close}){{id}}}}"),
+            json!({}),
+        ),
+        json!({"errors": [{"message": "The request nests too deeply to validate."}]})
+    );
+    let (open, close) = deep("{a:", "}", 50_000);
+    assert_eq!(
+        refused(
+            &format!("mutation{{updateProjectV2Field(input:{open}1{close}){{clientMutationId}}}}"),
+            json!({}),
+        ),
+        json!({"errors": [{"message": "The request nests too deeply to validate."}]})
+    );
+    let chain = (0..2_000)
+        .map(|at| format!("fragment f{at} on User{{...f{}}} ", at + 1))
+        .collect::<String>();
+    let cycle = refused(
+        &format!("query{{viewer{{...f0}}}} {chain} fragment f2000 on User{{...f0}}"),
+        json!({}),
+    );
+    assert!(
+        cycle["errors"][0]["message"].as_str().is_some_and(
+            |message| message.starts_with("Cannot spread fragment \"f0\" within itself via")
+        ),
+        "{cycle}"
+    );
+    let mut nested = json!("I_1");
+    for _ in 0..300 {
+        nested = json!([nested]);
+    }
+    let answered = refused("query($id:ID!){node(id:$id){id}}", json!({"id": nested}));
+    assert_eq!(
+        answered,
+        json!({"errors": [{"message": "Variables nest deeper than 200 levels"}]})
+    );
+    // A wide document that breaks nothing is not refused for its width.
+    let wide = (0..3_000)
+        .map(|at| format!("a{at}:login "))
+        .collect::<String>();
+    assert_eq!(
+        server.refuse(&json!({"query": format!("query{{viewer{{{wide}}}}}")})),
+        None
+    );
+    // A document that breaks no rule but holds more tokens than the check parses is refused
+    // unparsed, before any rule runs over it.
+    let oversized = "login ".repeat(200_000);
+    let answered = refused(&format!("query{{viewer{{{oversized}}}}}"), json!({}));
+    assert!(
+        answered["errors"][0]["message"]
+            .as_str()
+            .is_some_and(|message| message
+                .starts_with("Syntax Error: Document contains more than 200000 tokens.")),
+        "{answered}"
+    );

+/// The check's server stops when a client greets it with another protocol — as it does when its
+/// files change or it has been idle — and the next request after it stops is still answered, by
+/// a server started in its place, over connections this process held open to the one that
+/// stopped. A protocol it does not speak is answered `stale`, never served. Driven against a
+/// server of this test's own, through the same rendezvous every test process shares one by, so
+/// stopping it holds up no other test.
+///
+/// Bounded: two server starts and a stop take about a second, so a replacement that hangs fails
+/// this test within a minute rather than holding the run until its runner's timeout.
+#[test]
+fn a_stopped_schema_check_server_is_replaced_by_the_next_request() {
+    within(
+        std::time::Duration::from_secs(60),
+        "replacing a stopped schema check server",
+        a_stopped_server_is_replaced,
+    );
+}
+
+/// Runs `body` on a thread of its own and fails, naming `what`, when it has not finished within
+/// `limit`; a panic inside it fails the test as itself.
+fn within(limit: std::time::Duration, what: &str, body: impl FnOnce() + Send + 'static) {
+    use std::sync::mpsc::RecvTimeoutError;
+
+    let (done, finished) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
+    let worker = std::thread::spawn(move || {
+        body();
+        let _ = done.send(());
+    });
+    match finished.recv_timeout(limit) {
+        Ok(()) => worker.join().expect("the body finished"),
+        Err(RecvTimeoutError::Disconnected) => {
+            std::panic::resume_unwind(worker.join().expect_err("the body panicked"));
+        }
+        Err(RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) => panic!("{what} did not finish within {limit:?}"),
+    }
+}

+fn a_stopped_server_is_replaced() {
+    use serde_json::{Value, json};
+    use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Write};
+
+    let server = github_schema::serve_privately();
+    let (port, pid) = server.server();
+    let mut stream =

+/// Connects to the server at `port` and greets it with the protocol it speaks, answering the
+/// connection and the server's first line.
+fn greeted(port: u16) -> (std::net::TcpStream, serde_json::Value) {
+    use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Write};
+
+    let mut stream =
+        std::net::TcpStream::connect(("127.0.0.1", port)).expect("the server accepts a client");
+    stream
+        .write_all(b"{\"hello\":1}\n")
+        .expect("the hello is sent");
+    let mut answer = String::new();
+    BufReader::new(&stream)
+        .read_line(&mut answer)
+        .expect("the server answers the hello");
+    (
+        stream,
+        serde_json::from_str(&answer).expect("the answer is JSON"),
+    )
+}

+/// Waits, without connecting, until the server that wrote `endpoint` has removed it — which it
+/// does as it stops — and then that nothing listens on `port`. Connecting to poll would itself
+/// be the connection that keeps an idle server running.
+fn wait_until_stopped(endpoint: &std::path::Path, port: u16) {
+    let asked = std::time::Instant::now();
+    while endpoint.exists() {
+        assert!(
+            asked.elapsed() < std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),
+            "the server stopped and removed {}",
+            endpoint.display()
+        );
+        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(20));
+    }
+    while std::net::TcpStream::connect(("127.0.0.1", port)).is_ok() {
+        assert!(
+            asked.elapsed() < std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),
+            "the stopped server stopped listening"
+        );
+        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(20));
+    }
+}

+/// The answer to a field `User` does not have, named `field`, so each request is one no other
+/// test sends and no process has an answer to kept.
+fn unknown_user_field(server: &github_schema::PrivateServer, field: &str) {
+    use serde_json::json;
+
+    let query = format!("query{{viewer{{{field}}}}}");
+    let answered = server.refuse(&json!({ "query": query }));
+    let message = answered
+        .as_ref()
+        .and_then(|answered| answered["errors"][0]["message"].as_str());
+    assert_eq!(
+        message,
+        Some(format!("Cannot query field \"{field}\" on type \"User\".").as_str()),
+        "{answered:?}"
+    );
+}

+fn an_idle_server_stops() {
+    use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Write};
+
+    let idle = std::time::Duration::from_millis(500);
+    let server = github_schema::serve_privately_from_a_copy(idle);
+    let endpoint = server
+        .schema()
+        .parent()
+        .expect("the copy sits in the rendezvous directory")
+        .join("endpoint.json");
+    // `server()` holds this process's connection open, across four idle periods.
+    let (port, pid) = server.server();
+    std::thread::sleep(idle * 4);
+    unknown_user_field(&server, "heldAcrossIdlePeriods");
+    assert_eq!(
+        server.server(),
+        (port, pid),
+        "a connection held open keeps it serving"
+    );
+
+    // Every connection closed starts the count; one opened inside it cancels it.
+    server.disconnect();
+    std::thread::sleep(idle / 2);
+    let (mut stream, ready) = greeted(port);
+    assert_eq!(ready["ready"], true, "{ready}");
+    std::thread::sleep(idle * 4);
+    stream
+        .write_all(b"{\"query\":\"query{viewer{openedInsideTheCount}}\",\"operationName\":null,\"variables\":null,\"coerce\":false}\n")
+        .expect("the request is sent");
+    let mut answer = String::new();
+    BufReader::new(&stream)
+        .read_line(&mut answer)
+        .expect("a server whose stop was cancelled answers");
+    assert!(answer.contains("openedInsideTheCount"), "{answer}");
+    assert!(
+        endpoint.exists(),
+        "a server serving a client keeps its endpoint"
+    );
+
+    // The last connection closed, it stops by itself.
+    drop(stream);
+    wait_until_stopped(&endpoint, port);
+
+    unknown_user_field(&server, "askedAfterTheIdleStop");
+    let (_, replaced_by) = server.server();
+    assert_ne!(replaced_by, pid, "a new server answered");
+}

+fn a_changed_server_is_replaced() {
+    let server = github_schema::serve_privately_from_a_copy(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30));
+    let endpoint = server
+        .schema()
+        .parent()
+        .expect("the copy sits in the rendezvous directory")
+        .join("endpoint.json");
+    let (port, pid) = server.server();
+    unknown_user_field(&server, "beforeTheSchemaChanged");
+
+    // A comment changes the file and not the schema it describes.
+    let mut schema = std::fs::read(server.schema()).expect("the copy is read");
+    schema.extend_from_slice(b"\n# changed after the server started\n");
+    std::fs::write(server.schema(), schema).expect("the copy is changed");
+
+    let (_, stale) = greeted(port);
+    assert!(
+        stale["stale"]
+            .as_str()
+            .is_some_and(|why| why.contains(&server.schema().display().to_string())
+                && why.ends_with("changed since it started")),
+        "{stale}"
+    );
+    wait_until_stopped(&endpoint, port);
+
+    unknown_user_field(&server, "afterTheSchemaChanged");
+    let (_, replaced_by) = server.server();
+    assert_ne!(replaced_by, pid, "a new server answered");
+}

+/// A request line that is not the protocol's shape — not an object, a query that is not a
+/// string, an `operationName` that is neither a string nor null, a `coerce` missing or not a
+/// boolean — is answered `internal`, naming what is wrong, rather than read with defaults: a
+/// missing `coerce` read as false would skip the variables' coercion silently. The server goes on
+/// answering a well-formed request on the same connection.
+#[test]
+fn a_request_line_not_in_the_protocols_shape_is_answered_internal() {
+    use serde_json::{Value, json};
+    use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Write};
+
+    let server = github_schema::serve_privately();
+    let (port, _) = server.server();
+    let mut stream =
+        std::net::TcpStream::connect(("127.0.0.1", port)).expect("the server accepts a client");
+    stream
+        .set_read_timeout(Some(std::time::Duration::from_secs(60)))
+        .expect("a read timeout");
+    let mut reader = BufReader::new(stream.try_clone().expect("a second handle"));
+    let mut exchange = |line: &str| -> Value {
+        stream
+            .write_all(format!("{line}\n").as_bytes())
+            .expect("the line is sent");
+        let mut answer = String::new();
+        reader.read_line(&mut answer).expect("the server answers");
+        serde_json::from_str(&answer).expect("the answer is JSON")
+    };
+    assert_eq!(exchange(r#"{"hello":1}"#)["ready"], json!(true));
+
+    let valid =
+        r#""query":"query($id:ID!){node(id:$id){id}}","operationName":null,"variables":{"id":5.5}"#;
+    for (line, named) in [
+        ("null".to_owned(), "a request is a JSON object"),
+        ("[1]".to_owned(), "a request is a JSON object"),
+        (
+            r#"{"query":5,"operationName":null,"variables":{},"coerce":true}"#.to_owned(),
+            "a request's query is a string",
+        ),
+        (
+            r#"{"query":"query{viewer{login}}","operationName":3,"variables":{},"coerce":true}"#
+                .to_owned(),
+            "a request's operationName is a string or null",
+        ),
+        (
+            format!("{{{valid}}}"),
+            "a request's coerce is true or false",
+        ),
+        (
+            format!(r#"{{{valid},"coerce":"yes"}}"#),
+            "a request's coerce is true or false",
+        ),
+    ] {
+        let answer = exchange(&line);
+        assert!(
+            answer["internal"]
+                .as_str()
+                .is_some_and(|internal| internal.contains(named)),
+            "{line} was answered {answer}"
+        );
+        assert!(
+            answer.get("errors").is_none(),
+            "{line} was answered {answer}"
+        );
+    }
+
+    // The same request, whole, has its variables coerced: an `ID` is a string or an integer.
+    let answer = exchange(&format!(r#"{{{valid},"coerce":true}}"#));
+    assert!(
+        answer["errors"][0]["message"]
+            .as_str()
+            .is_some_and(|message| message.contains("$id")),
+        "{answer}"
+    );
+}

+LeaseId = NewType('LeaseId', str)
+LeaseTitle = NewType('LeaseTitle', str)

+class LeaseIssue(TypedDict):
+    id: LeaseId
+    title: LeaseTitle
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class LeaseRead:
+    """`issue(id:)`, what `--release-leases` asks of each recorded lease."""
+    id: LeaseId
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class LeaseUpdate:
+    """`issueUpdate`, the one write `--release-leases` sends: the lease and its new title."""
+    id: LeaseId
+    title: LeaseTitle
+
+
+def read_lease_request(value: object) -> LeaseRead | LeaseUpdate:
+    """The janitor's request, its whole shape checked rather than assumed."""
+    assert isinstance(value, dict), value
+    query, variables = value.get('query'), value.get('variables')
+    assert isinstance(query, str) and isinstance(variables, dict), value
+    identifier = variables.get('id')
+    assert isinstance(identifier, str) and identifier, variables
+    if 'issueUpdate(' in query:
+        assert set(variables) == {'id', 'input'}, variables
+        update = variables['input']
+        assert isinstance(update, dict) and set(update) == {'title'}, update
+        title = update['title']
+        assert isinstance(title, str) and title, update
+        return LeaseUpdate(LeaseId(identifier), LeaseTitle(title))
+    assert 'issue(id:$id)' in query and set(variables) == {'id'}, value
+    return LeaseRead(LeaseId(identifier))
+
+
+class LeaseFault(StrEnum):
+    UNIDENTIFIED_READ = auto()
+    NO_ISSUE = auto()
+    UNCONFIRMED_RELEASE = auto()
+
+
+class RecordsPath(StrEnum):
+    """What stands at the path `--release-leases` is given."""
+    DIRECTORY = auto()
+    ABSENT = auto()
+    FILE = auto()
+
+
+@dataclass
+class LeaseTeam:
+    """What the stand-in Linear holds of the pool's lease issues, and what it was asked."""
+    issues: dict[LeaseId, LeaseTitle]
+    fault: LeaseFault | None = None
+    reads: list[LeaseId] = field(default_factory=list)
+    updates: list[LeaseUpdate] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+    def answer(self, request: LeaseRead | LeaseUpdate) -> dict[str, object]:
+        match request:
+            case LeaseUpdate():
+                self.updates.append(request)
+                if self.fault is LeaseFault.UNCONFIRMED_RELEASE:
+                    return {'data': {'issueUpdate': {'success': False}}}
+                self.issues[request.id] = request.title
+                return {'data': {'issueUpdate': {'success': True}}}
+            case LeaseRead():
+                self.reads.append(request.id)
+                title = self.issues.get(request.id)
+                match self.fault:
+                    case LeaseFault.UNIDENTIFIED_READ:
+                        return {'data': {'issue': {'title': title}}}
+                    case LeaseFault.NO_ISSUE:
+                        return {'data': {}}
+                    case _:
+                        issue: LeaseIssue | None = None if title is None else LeaseIssue(id=request.id, title=title)
+                        return {'data': {'issue': issue}}

+class LeaseJourneys(unittest.TestCase):
+    """`--linear --release-leases DIR`: a cancelled job hands back what it recorded, only that."""

+    PREFIX = 'onetaskgraph live cleanup lease-v1 TEST plugin '
+
+    def release(self, team: LeaseTeam, records: dict[str, str],
+                path: RecordsPath = RecordsPath.DIRECTORY) -> tuple[subprocess.CompletedProcess[str], Path]:
+        class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+            def log_message(self, *_args: object) -> None:
+                pass
+
+            def do_POST(self) -> None:
+                assert self.headers['Authorization'] == 'offline-linear-key'
+                request = read_lease_request(json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers['Content-Length']))))
+                body = json.dumps(team.answer(request)).encode()
+                self.send_response(200)
+                self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
+                self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(body)))
+                self.end_headers()
+                self.wfile.write(body)
+
+        server = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), Handler)
+        thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever)
+        thread.start()
+        directory = Path(os.environ.get('TMPDIR', '/tmp')) / f'lease-records-{os.getpid()}-{time.monotonic_ns()}'
+        match path:
+            case RecordsPath.DIRECTORY:
+                directory.mkdir(parents=True)
+                for name, content in records.items():
+                    (directory / f'{name}.json').write_text(content)
+            case RecordsPath.FILE:
+                directory.write_text('not a directory of lease records')
+            case RecordsPath.ABSENT:
+                pass
+        try:
+            environment = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items()
+                           if not key.startswith(('LINEAR_', 'GH_', 'GITHUB_'))}
+            environment.update(LINEAR_API_KEY='offline-linear-key', LINEAR_WRITE_TEAM='test')
+            result = subprocess.run(
+                [os.environ['JANITOR_BINARY'], '--linear', '--release-leases', str(directory),
+                 '--loopback', f'http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}'],
+                env=environment, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
+        finally:
+            server.shutdown()
+            server.server_close()
+            thread.join()
+        return result, directory

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Hold scripts/check-npm-publish.sh to never writing the checkout it runs from.
+#
+# That check needs a TypeScript SDK `dist` to pack, and once wrote a stand-in into the
+# checkout's sdks/typescript when there was none, removing it on exit. distribution-test runs
+# it beside github-workflows:cd-journeys, whose publish build writes the real `dist` into the
+# same directory and reads it back — so a build that landed between the two was deleted under
+# the journey, which failed ENOENT on sdks/typescript/dist/index.js on the hosted Linux job.
+# Whether that happens is a matter of timing, so this does not wait for the race: it runs the
+# check in a scratch clone holding no `dist` and refuses any change to the clone's
+# sdks/typescript at all, which the stand-in's create and removal always make.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+fatal() {
+  echo "check-npm-publish-leaves-checkout: $1" >&2
+  echo "check-npm-publish-leaves-checkout: next: $2" >&2
+  exit 1
+}
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)" || fatal \
+  "could not resolve this repository's root from ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" \
+  "run it from a checkout of this repository, as 'just script-check' does"
+readonly ROOT
+
+PYTHON="$(command -v python3)" || fatal "python3 is not on PATH" "run 'just bootstrap', then rerun"
+# Absolute, so a relative PATH entry still names it once this is inside the clone (AGENTS.md).
+case "$PYTHON" in
+  /*) ;;
+  *) PYTHON="$(cd "$(dirname "$PYTHON")" && pwd)/$(basename "$PYTHON")" ;;
+esac
+
+scratch="$(mktemp -d)" || fatal "could not create a scratch directory" \
+  "check the permissions of \$TMPDIR and 'df -h' for free space, then rerun"
+trap 'rm -rf "$scratch"' EXIT
+
+# The path below is built from $ROOT at run time, so ShellCheck cannot follow it.
+# shellcheck source=scripts/scratch-clone.sh
+if [ ! -r "$ROOT/scripts/scratch-clone.sh" ] || ! source "$ROOT/scripts/scratch-clone.sh"; then
+  fatal "could not load $ROOT/scripts/scratch-clone.sh, which strips the git environment" \
+    "restore that file with 'git checkout -- scripts/scratch-clone.sh' and rerun"
+fi
+
+# A clone, because the check copies what its checkout tracks, overlaid with the working
+# tree's own files so what is under test is the scripts as they are now.
+scratch_clone "$ROOT" "$scratch/repo" || fatal "could not clone $ROOT" "fix what is reported above, then rerun"
+copy_tracked_files "$ROOT" "$scratch/repo" scripts npm sdks/typescript || fatal \
+  "could not copy the working tree's scripts, npm and sdks/typescript into the clone" \
+  "confirm 'git ls-files' answers in $ROOT and 'df -h' for free space, then rerun"
+sdk="$scratch/repo/sdks/typescript"
+[ ! -e "$sdk/dist" ] || fatal "the clone already holds $sdk/dist, so the case below proves nothing" \
+  "check that sdks/typescript/dist is not tracked ('git ls-files sdks/typescript/dist'), then rerun"
+
+snapshot() {
+  "$PYTHON" - "$sdk" <<'PY'
+import os
+import sys
+
+root = sys.argv[1]
+for directory, names, files in os.walk(root):
+    names.sort()
+    for name in [directory, *(os.path.join(directory, f) for f in sorted(files))]:
+        info = os.stat(name)
+        print(os.path.relpath(name, root).replace(os.sep, "/"), info.st_size, info.st_mtime_ns)
+PY
+}
+

+  fatal "scripts/check-npm-publish.sh failed in the clone, so whether it leaves its checkout alone is unknown" \
+    "fix what it reports above, then rerun"
+fi

+
+if ! diff -u "$scratch/before" "$scratch/after" > "$scratch/diff"; then
+  sed 's/^/check-npm-publish-leaves-checkout:   /' "$scratch/diff" >&2

+fi
